# the contributor audit: projected counts, convex-position clusters, and simplex slices

The three source notes below pass a full proof read. This is an audit of
their stated auxiliary results, not a proof of unrestricted OC.

## Actual counting roof

In `candidate 0d7a19234146a56a`,
the final affine roof has radius one through base N-1 and epsilon at N.
Thus the listed N+1 fibers are exactly the actual integer sections.
The density N 1_T+1_(epsilon T) is an exact finite indicator sum.
The six barycentric thresholds sum to one, so their halfspaces cover
all continuous space. Their tiny-simplex traces are respectively full
and empty by strict inequalities. The two difference-of-powers bounds
are valid with the stated 4/5 and 6/7 endpoints. In particular
Gamma_5-648/2401=2464277/18670176>0, proving an all-point upper bound
strictly below Gamma_5. The common large-simplex core separately gives
the claimed lower bound above Gamma_5/2. Neither inequality identifies
the exact ordinary maximum. The displayed strict midpoint violation
also rules out log-concavity after any null-set change of density.

## Arbitrary clusters and actual parity

In `candidate 32c90486ff8c59d7`,
the six canonical through-centroid caps contain exactly one cluster
each. For an arbitrary nonzero through-centroid affine margin, the six
vertex values sum to zero; if their maximum is m, every value is at
least -5m. The maximizing cluster is therefore entirely in the positive
halfspace when delta<1/5. This proves the exact ordinary maximum 1/6.
The center used for this ordinary lower bound is not asserted to lie
in the disconnected mixture support.

For actual sources, a positive full-dimensional convex fiber having
zero measure outside the closed cluster union is wholly contained in
that union: otherwise its interior and then closure contradict the
measure assertion. Connectedness places it in one component. Two
different labels in one integer parity class force a positive-volume
Minkowski midpoint at an integer base. Every barycentric coordinate
there is at most 1/2+d delta/(d+1), strictly below the required large
coordinate 1-delta/(d+1) of every cluster. Thus it is outside the union.
This proves k<=2^n for the specified simplex-vertex neighborhoods,
including alternative decompositions into actual fibers. It does not
bound arbitrary disconnected support components or prove a quantitative
mass allocation for clusters with positive connecting volume.

## Ambient simplex normal form and exact caps

In `candidate 56a670ccbde263ec`,
the barycentric coordinate map fixes the entire integer base. Its
determinant equals the ratio of the selected base-simplex determinant
to the ambient simplex determinant. Therefore its single continuous
d-dimensional Jacobian is n!|Q|/((n+d)!|C|). This proves normalized
depth invariance only for the stipulated positive full-d measure.
For q<d, differently oriented affine fibers can acquire different
H_q Jacobians; the source explicitly excludes that inference.

The divided-difference tail has the correct normalization from uniform
barycentric density (d+1)!. Differentiation yields the stated slice
coefficient, and duplicating a knot gives the factor 1/(d+2) in the
moment formula by integrating its barycentric splitting interval.
The inward limits at repeated extreme knots are necessary and equal
the volumes and moments of actual closed endpoint faces. The canonical
cap identity follows from homothety at the vertex while keeping the
original integer index in the sum, including vertical boundary mass.

For arbitrary caps, the two positive radial sums in the projective
product parametrization agree. Their remaining normalization t L=1
gives L^{-(d+1)} after both simplex-coordinate Jacobians, exactly as
in the source. Multiplication by positive L turns the original ambient
cap into one linear product inequality. No independent thresholds are
introduced. Interior and endpoint limits for nonvertical caps have null
d-dimensional boundaries; vertical caps retain their closed indicators.

The explicit nonhomothetic fibers at bases 1,2,3 follow directly from
the two roof inequalities. Their endpoint and middle volumes and sum
moments give q=310337/387828 for d=5, epsilon=1/10. The through-centroid
cap contains the two endpoints and qT in the middle, so the exact gap
below Gamma_5 is valid. The separate own-middle-centroid estimate
59375/157464 is above Gamma_5/2 and controls every ambient halfspace.
The example only obstructs transferring the ordinary centroid bound.

## Verification

Reran `supporting computation verify_projected_count_density_and_cluster_obstruction.py`:
PASS 4,700 exact checks. Reran `supporting computation verify_ambient_simplex_slice_cap_calculus.py`:
PASS 234 exact checks. The independent Helly audit of the simplex note
also passes and supplies a direct projective slice/cap cross-check.
These computations supplement the proofs above; they do not replace
any all-dimensional or all-halfspace step.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
